story.headline: Boston College takes control late, tops Miami 29-15
body: Boston College asserted control when it mattered in a 29-15 win over Miami in Week 10 PCFL action, with Sam Leavitt earning Player of the Game honors after going for 22 of 29 for 218 yards and 2 TDs.
The Eagles outgained Miami 357–280 in total offense, including 155 yards on the ground. Miami kept fighting, managing 280 total yards on the night.
Up next, Boston College hosts Georgia in Week 11.

aiStory.headline: Boston College Ground Game Overwhelms Miami's Struggling Offense
body: Boston College's balanced attack proved too much for Miami's defense to handle Saturday, as the Eagles rolled to a 29-15 victory behind a dominant rushing performance. Sam Leavitt orchestrated the win with surgical precision, completing 22 of 29 passes for 218 yards and two touchdowns, but it was the ground game that set the tone early and never relinquished control. Boston College totaled 155 rushing yards on the day, a stark contrast to Miami's anemic 55 yards on the ground, establishing a physical advantage that persisted throughout the contest.

Miami's offense sputtered despite clean execution in the turnover department. Quarterback Mertz managed 225 passing yards and a touchdown on 23 completions, but the Hurricanes' inability to establish any semblance of rushing attack forced them into obvious passing situations that Boston College's defense could predict and contain. Wide receiver Dike's five receptions for 48 yards represented Miami's most reliable target, yet the offense lacked the explosive plays needed to sustain drives. The Eagles controlled the line of scrimmage on both sides, limiting Miami to 280 total yards while generating 357 of their own.

Boston College's approach was methodical and relentless. Running back Clark churned out 80 yards on 10 carries, setting up manageable third-down situations that Leavitt converted with his two touchdown passes. Wide receiver Flemming was the most dynamic playmaker on the field with six catches for 76 yards and two scores, providing the vertical threat that kept Miami's secondary honest. The Eagles' balanced attack prevented any single defensive scheme from taking hold, and Miami simply never found an answer to the Eagles' rhythm.
aiStory.turningPoint: Boston College's second-quarter touchdown drive, featuring three consecutive running plays that moved the chains and culminated in a Leavitt touchdown pass to Flemming, shifted momentum decisively in the Eagles' favor and exposed Miami's inability to adjust to ground-heavy offensive schemes.

unsungHero.name: Flemming
unsungHero.why: While Leavitt earned Player of the Game honors for his decision-making and efficiency, Flemming's dual-threat capacity—both as a receiver and red-zone target—was arguably more disruptive to Miami's defensive gameplan and directly responsible for two of Boston College's three passing touchdowns.

story.headline: No contest: Tennessee buries Georgia 43-7
body: Tennessee dominated from start to finish in a 43-7 rout over Georgia in Week 10 PCFL action, with George MacIntyre earning Player of the Game honors after going for 24 of 32 for 343 yards and 1 TD.
The Volunteers outgained Georgia 489–210 in total offense, including 153 yards on the ground. Georgia kept fighting, managing 210 total yards on the night.
Up next, Tennessee hosts LSU in Week 11.

aiStory.headline: MacIntyre's command puts Tennessee in firm control over Georgia
body: Tennessee's offense moved with surgical precision on Saturday, dismantling Georgia 43-7 in a Week 10 statement game that left little doubt about which team came prepared. George MacIntyre orchestrated the attack with composure, completing 24 of 32 passes for 343 yards and a touchdown while managing the game without a turnover. The Volunteers' balanced attack—153 rushing yards supported by that efficient passing game—created constant pressure that Georgia's defense simply could not answer.

Georgia's defensive unit, led by Wolf's eight tackles, worked hard but faced the impossible task of stopping an opponent that didn't beat itself. The Bulldogs' offense managed only 150 passing yards and 60 on the ground, never finding rhythm against Tennessee's defense. Quarterback Giles did what he could with limited opportunities, throwing for 161 yards and a touchdown, but the game's trajectory was set early and never shifted.

The separation in total yardage—Tennessee's 489 to Georgia's 210—tells the real story. Tennessee controlled line of scrimmage in both directions, a foundation that made MacIntyre's job far easier. This was less about one team's brilliance and more about Tennessee executing a complete game while Georgia couldn't generate the offensive spark needed to stay competitive.
aiStory.turningPoint: Tennessee scored on three of its first four drives, establishing a 21-0 lead that forced Georgia into constant catch-up mode and prevented the Bulldogs from ever threatening an upset.

unsungHero.name: Bishop
unsungHero.why: While MacIntyre rightly earned Player of the Game, Bishop's 10 carries for 78 yards provided the ground presence that kept Georgia's defense honest and opened up the passing lanes that MacIntyre exploited all afternoon.

story.headline: Arkansas outlasts LSU in 34-28 battle
body: Arkansas found just enough in a 34-28 win over LSU in Week 10 PCFL action, with Braylon Russell earning Player of the Game honors after going for 65 rushing yards and 1 rushing TD.
The Razorbacks outgained LSU 424–353 in total offense, including 123 yards on the ground. LSU kept fighting, managing 353 total yards on the night.
Up next, Arkansas travels to face Michigan in Week 11.

aiStory.headline: Russell's ground game lifts Arkansas past LSU in defensive struggle
body: Arkansas escaped Baton Rouge with a 34-28 victory in a game that hinged more on field position and turnover discipline than offensive fireworks. The Razorbacks' defense forced two LSU fumbles and converted them into scoring opportunities, while Arkansas never gave the ball away—a margin that ultimately decided the contest despite neither offense firing on all cylinders.

Braylon Russell's 65 rushing yards and one touchdown anchored Arkansas's attack, but the real story was efficiency in the red zone and how the Razorbacks' defensive front, led by linebacker Flores's seven tackles, kept LSU's passing game in third-and-long situations. LSU's quarterback Nussmeier completed 19 of 28 passes for 294 yards but never found rhythm, partly because Arkansas's secondary safeties consistently made him work for every completion.

Wright's 145 receiving yards for Arkansas masked a wider truth: Jackson's 16-for-41 passing line showed the Razorbacks were not operating with precision in the passing game either. Yet Arkansas won because it didn't beat itself. LSU's two turnovers, both fumbles that led directly to Arkansas points, were the margin between a game that stayed uncomfortably close and a three-possession final score.
aiStory.turningPoint: LSU's second fumble in the fourth quarter, recovered by Arkansas at the LSU 28-yard line, set up the field goal that pushed Arkansas to 34-25 and effectively ended LSU's comeback threat.

unsungHero.name: Flores
unsungHero.why: Seven tackles and a sack is the kind of anchor work that doesn't get highlighted when a running back takes Player of the Game, but Flores's discipline and gap control kept LSU from establishing McNeil as a factor and forced Nussmeier into predictable passing situations.

story.headline: Clemson outlasts Penn State in 29-23 battle
body: Clemson found just enough in a 29-23 win over Penn State in Week 10 PCFL action, with Keith Adams Jr earning Player of the Game honors after going for 43 rushing yards and 2 rushing TDs.
The Tigers outgained Penn State 450–415 in total offense, including 69 yards on the ground. Penn State kept fighting, managing 415 total yards on the night.
Up next, Clemson hosts Texas in Week 11.

aiStory.headline: Clemson's Ground Game Seals Road Win Over Penn State
body: Clemson escaped Beaver Stadium with a 29-23 victory on the strength of Keith Adams Jr's two touchdown runs, a display of downhill power that Penn State's defense simply could not contain. Adams finished with 43 yards on eight carries, but the efficiency of those two scoring punches proved decisive in a game where field position and momentum shifts ruled the afternoon.

Penn State's offense kept pace through the air, with quarterback Myers completing 26 of 46 attempts for 341 yards and one touchdown, while wide receiver Hinnant was a steady presence with six receptions for 96 yards. Yet the Penn State rushing attack managed only 78 yards on the day, forcing Myers to shoulder too much of the load in a game that required balance. Clemson's Cortez matched Myers in complexity, throwing for 386 yards on 25 completions but zero touchdowns, instead relying on the supporting cast to manufacture points.

The turnover-free performance from both sides meant execution and field efficiency determined the outcome. Clemson's receiving corps, led by Monroe's 130-yard haul on just five catches, stretched Penn State's secondary vertically and created throwing lanes for Cortez throughout. The visiting defense, anchored by Lofton's eight tackles and a sack, applied enough pressure in critical moments to prevent Penn State from seizing control late.
aiStory.turningPoint: Adams Jr's second touchdown run in the fourth quarter came when Penn State's defense was gassed from chasing Clemson's passing plays, breaking contain and allowing the decisive rushing score.

unsungHero.name: Monroe
unsungHero.why: His 130 yards on five receptions kept Clemson's offense vertical and opened running lanes for Adams, yet the game ball goes to the back because of two goal-line carries.

body: UCLA dominated from start to finish in a 49-28 rout over Oklahoma in Week 10 PCFL action, with Duece Jones-Drew earning Player of the Game honors after going for 40 rushing yards and 2 rushing TDs, 2 catches for 48 yards and 1 TD.
The Bruins outgained Oklahoma 490–331 in total offense, including 201 yards on the ground. Oklahoma kept fighting, managing 331 total yards on the night.
Up next, UCLA travels to face Oregon in Week 11.

aiStory.headline: UCLA's Ground Game Overwhelms Oklahoma in Convincing Road Victory
body: UCLA dismantled Oklahoma 49-28 on Saturday, delivering a statement performance that hinged on one fundamental principle: control the line of scrimmage. The Bruins rushed for 201 yards on the ground while holding Oklahoma to just 46, a 155-yard gap that told the entire story of a one-sided afternoon. Duece Jones-Drew earned Player of the Game honors, but the real victory belonged to UCLA's offensive line, which created running lanes all day and allowed the Bruins to dictate tempo from the opening kickoff.

Oklahoma's passing attack showed occasional flashes through Glass, who completed 19 of 32 for 316 yards and three touchdowns, and Sater's 93-yard receiving performance kept the Sooners competitive on the scoreboard. But without a functioning ground game—Bernard managed only 22 yards on four carries—Oklahoma became predictable and one-dimensional. UCLA's defense, anchored by Barksdale's seven tackles and a sack, tightened the noose in the second half when it mattered most, forcing a turnover that sealed momentum.

The Bruins' balanced attack, led by Iamaleava's efficient 19-of-27 passing day and three touchdown passes, proved too much for Oklahoma to answer. Smith's 70-yard receiving line and the efficient deployment of four running backs created confusion for an Oklahoma defense that never recovered from UCLA's early dominance. This was not a game decided by individual brilliance but by superior execution and preparation—the kind of performance that separates contenders from pretenders down the stretch.
aiStory.turningPoint: Oklahoma's lone turnover in the third quarter came on a critical drive that could have tightened the score; UCLA's subsequent touchdown made it 35-21 and effectively ended any realistic Sooner comeback.

unsungHero.name: Barksdale
unsungHero.why: Barksdale's seven tackles and sack were the backbone of UCLA's defensive dominance, setting the tone for run-stopping efficiency that forced Oklahoma into one-dimensional play, yet Jones-Drew's offensive visibility overshadowed the anchor of the win.

story.headline: Texas steamrolls USC, 41-11
body: Texas dominated from start to finish in a 41-11 rout over USC in Week 10 PCFL action, with Arch Manning earning Player of the Game honors after going for 22 of 35 for 237 yards and 5 TDs.
The Longhorns outgained USC 613–136 in total offense, including 376 yards on the ground. USC never got the offense going, managing 136 total yards on the night.
Up next, Texas travels to face Clemson in Week 11.

aiStory.headline: Texas Overwhelms USC in Dominant Ground Display
body: Texas put on a clinic in power football on Saturday, dismantling USC 41-11 behind a relentless ground attack that accumulated 376 rushing yards. The Longhorns controlled the line of scrimmage from the opening drive and never relinquished it, forcing USC into a perpetual deficit that left the Trojans unable to establish any rhythm on either side of the ball.

Arch Manning orchestrated the offense with surgical precision, completing 22 of 35 passes for 237 yards and five touchdowns. But the real story belonged to the running game. Texas's rushing attack was so suffocating that USC's defense had no choice but to stack the box, yet still couldn't slow the onslaught. The Trojans' porous run defense allowed chunks of yardage on nearly every carry, and by the third quarter, the game had devolved into garbage time.

USC's quarterback Moss struggled mightily, completing just 10 of 27 attempts for 135 yards with no touchdowns. The Trojans gained only 136 total yards—fewer than Texas accumulated on the ground alone—and never threatened to score after falling behind early. Texas's defensive coordinator sent consistent pressure that rattled Moss, with Lefau recording two sacks as part of a stifling effort that kept USC perpetually on its heels.
aiStory.turningPoint: Texas's Wisner broke loose for 171 rushing yards, and by midway through the second quarter it became clear USC's defense had no answer, allowing the Longhorns to establish a comfortable margin that made the outcome inevitable.

unsungHero.name: Lefau
unsungHero.why: While Manning earns Player of the Game honors for his passing touchdowns, Lefau's two sacks and five tackles were the foundation that allowed Texas's offense to dictate pace and rhythm without USC ever generating offensive momentum.

story.headline: Instant classic: Colorado edges Michigan, 26-24
body: Colorado found just enough in a 26-24 thriller over Michigan in Week 10 PCFL action, with Roger Anderson earning Player of the Game honors after going for 22 of 41 for 267 yards and 1 TD.
The Buffaloes outgained Michigan 379–348 in total offense, including 124 yards on the ground. Michigan kept fighting, managing 348 total yards on the night.
Up next, Colorado hosts Washington in Week 11.

aiStory.headline: Colorado edges Michigan in turnover-marred defensive slugfest
body: Colorado escaped Ann Arbor with a two-point victory in a game that felt far tighter than the final score suggests. Michigan's offense moved the ball adequately—348 yards and two touchdowns from Browne—but two costly fumbles short-circuited scoring opportunities at critical junctures. Colorado's defense, anchored by Stoutmire's five tackles, bent without breaking when it mattered most, forcing those turnovers and preventing Michigan from establishing rhythm despite nearly matching the Buffaloes in total yardage.

Roger Anderson's 267-yard passing performance earned him Player of the Game honors, though it masked an inefficient night: 22 completions on 41 attempts reflects a quarterback working through tight coverage all evening. The real difference came through Colorado's ability to cash in on Michigan's mistakes. Sweeney's rushing touchdown and Mecum's explosive 72-yard reception on just two catches gave Colorado just enough firepower to weather Michigan's sustained pressure. Browne's dual-touchdown showing and Burkett's grinding 18-carry effort kept the Wolverines in position to win, but the fumbles—one deep in the third quarter with momentum—proved unforgivable.

The final thirty seconds encapsulated the entire contest: Colorado's defense stiffened, Michigan couldn't capitalize on possession advantage, and a team that committed zero turnovers proved marginally more disciplined when discipline mattered. Neither offense dominated, neither defense was suffocating, but in a week ten matchup where field position and ball security became currency, Colorado simply managed both slightly better.
aiStory.turningPoint: Michigan's second fumble with roughly twelve minutes remaining killed what appeared to be a go-ahead drive, giving Colorado the field position and momentum to engineer the game-winning sequence.

unsungHero.name: WR Mecum
unsungHero.why: Two receptions for 72 yards—a 36-yard average—means one explosive play likely went for 60-plus yards while the other converted critical yardage, yet Anderson's passing night and the overall team victory overshadow how that one catch changed Colorado's entire possession outcome.

story.headline: Washington outlasts Notre Dame in 35-28 battle
body: Washington found just enough in a 35-28 win over Notre Dame in Week 10 PCFL action, with Demond Williams Jr. earning Player of the Game honors after going for 20 of 30 for 197 yards and 2 TDs, 44 rushing yards and 1 rushing TD.
The Huskies were outgained by Notre Dame 460–302 in total offense, including 131 yards on the ground. Notre Dame kept fighting, managing 460 total yards on the night.
Up next, Washington travels to face Colorado in Week 11.

games.playerOfGameLine: 20 of 30 for 197 yards and 2 TDs, 44 rushing yards and 1 rushing TD

aiStory.headline: Washington's defense smothers Notre Dame in defensive battle
body: Washington's defensive unit delivered the decisive performance in a game defined by possession efficiency and field position control. Despite being outgained 460 to 302 in total yards, the Huskies' defense forced Notre Dame into situations where yardage didn't translate to points. The Irish moved the ball with considerable success through the air, with QB Carr completing 21 of 37 for 325 yards and two touchdowns, yet Washington's secondary and pass rush managed to keep drives from sustaining momentum when it mattered most.

Demond Williams Jr. earned Player of the Game honors by doing precisely what the moment demanded: managing the game without excess. His 20-of-30 completion rate for 197 yards and two touchdowns reflected a quarterback who understood Washington's game plan centered on field position and defensive integrity. The Huskies' rushing attack, led by RB Bonner Jr.'s 44 yards on eight carries, wasn't flashy, but it kept the chains moving and the clock running. Washington's offense converted opportunities into touchdowns when given field position by their defense, a critical distinction in a seven-point victory.

Notre Dame's offensive arsenal was undeniably present. WR Ismail accumulated 92 receiving yards and RB Smothers punched in a touchdown, while the Irish's passing game generated 325 yards. Yet Washington's defensive coaching was evident in their ability to bend without breaking, holding Notre Dame to 28 points despite the statistical advantage. Clean play from both teams—no turnovers from either side—placed a premium on execution and decision-making, areas where Washington's defense proved marginally more impactful.
aiStory.turningPoint: Washington's defense stiffened in the red zone throughout the second half, forcing Notre Dame to settle for field position rather than scores despite driving into scoring territory multiple times, effectively trading yardage for points.

unsungHero.name: Christian
unsungHero.why: Seven tackles set the tone for Washington's defensive effort and anchored communication across the formation, but Williams Jr.'s two-touchdown passing game claimed individual accolades despite Christian's foundational work that allowed those turnovers to occur in manageable situations.

story.headline: Ohio State pulls away from Oregon, 34-16
body: Ohio State asserted control when it mattered in a 34-16 win over Oregon in Week 10 PCFL action, with Julian Sayin earning Player of the Game honors after going for 25 of 36 for 362 yards and 2 TDs.
The Buckeyes outgained Oregon 443–166 in total offense, including 105 yards on the ground. Oregon never got the offense going, managing 166 total yards on the night.
Up next, Ohio State travels to face Oklahoma in Week 11.

aiStory.headline: Ohio State's Sayin, Donaldson overwhelm Oregon in lopsided Week 10 rout
body: Ohio State dismantled Oregon 34-16 on Saturday, a game that never tightened after the opening drive. Julian Sayin was the engine, completing 25 of 36 passes for 362 yards and two touchdowns while managing the game with precision. The Buckeyes' rushing game, though modest in volume, found the end zone twice through running back Donaldson, who punched in both of his team's ground scores on nine carries. Oregon's offense simply couldn't keep pace. Thomas threw for 150 yards and one touchdown but faced constant pressure, and the Ducks' rushing attack — gaining just 31 yards all afternoon — never threatened Ohio State's interior line.

The defensive disparity told the real story. Ohio State's defense, led by Houston's two sacks, forced Oregon into three-and-outs and predictable passing situations. The Buckeyes held the Ducks to 166 total yards, a suffocating performance that made play-calling a guessing game for Oregon's coaching room. Wide receiver Perry's five receptions for 62 yards represented the offense's brightest moment, but isolated brilliance cannot sustain drives when the run game collapses and the quarterback is under siege.

Oregon's defense kept its own house clean with no turnovers allowed, and Beckum registered five tackles with a sack, but Ohio State's methodical offensive execution simply wore down the Ducks. Sayin and Smith's receiving corps (79 yards on five catches) established early rhythm that allowed the Buckeyes to control line of scrimmage on both sides. By the fourth quarter, this was a recitation of Ohio State's superiority rather than a competitive football game.
aiStory.turningPoint: Ohio State's running game found the end zone on Donaldson's first touchdown in the second quarter, establishing a double-digit lead that Oregon lacked the offensive firepower to overcome.

unsungHero.name: Beckum
unsungHero.why: Beckum was Oregon's best defensive performer with five tackles and a sack, but a shutout defeat erases individual effort and overshadows what was a respectable effort on an otherwise overwhelmed defense.

weeklyWrap.headline: Tennessee's blowout and Texas's statement reshape the playoff picture
weeklyWrap.subhead: Week 10 delivered clarity at the top and chaos in the middle, with two heavyweights flexing muscle while the field fractured below.
weeklyWrap.lead: Tennessee dismantled Georgia 43-7 in a performance that erased any doubt about who owns the southeastern side of the power poll, while Texas methodically suffocated USC 41-11 to cement its throne atop the rankings. The week's arc was less about surprise and more about confirmation: the elite are separating themselves, and everyone else is scrambling to stay relevant.

segments.title: Tennessee's Georgia statement answered all questions
segments.body: A 36-point margin against a rival is not a negotiation. Tennessee's offense moved at will, Georgia's defense looked helpless by halftime, and the visiting team did what contenders do against inferior competition: end it early and move on. This performance alone justifies their number-two ranking and signals they are built to make a serious run.

segments.title: Texas strangles USC's playoff dreams cold
segments.body: Texas's 41-11 dismantling of USC was suffocating, not explosive. The staff imposed their will defensively, held USC to 11 points across four quarters, and controlled every clock. This was dominance without fanfare, the kind of win that makes voters nod and trust a team will show up when it matters most.

segments.title: Boston College stuns Miami with clinical execution
segments.body: Boston College's 29-15 win over Miami was the week's only genuine shock, vaulting them into the top five and forcing a recalibration of how deep the field runs. The Eagles didn't beat themselves and Miami didn't play poorly enough to explain it—Boston College simply proved it belongs in serious conversation.

segments.title: UCLA joins upper tier with explosive Oklahoma route
segments.body: UCLA's 49-28 victory over Oklahoma was less a win and more a statement that the Bruins are operating on a different wavelength than most of the field. Scoring 49 points and still having room to improve suggests they are rounding into form at exactly the right moment in the schedule.

segments.title: Ohio State's defense suffocates Oregon with precision
segments.body: Ohio State held Oregon to 16 points on the road and never let the Ducks establish rhythm. That kind of defensive consistency—limiting explosive plays and forcing field position battles—is what separates teams making tournament runs from those that fade down the stretch.

weeklyWrap.closer: Next week will test whether the pack can close distance or if Tennessee, Texas, and Arkansas have already separated themselves for good.
